newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville lifts prices for off-peak power.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville lifts prices for off-peak power.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) raised next-day offer prices for both firm and non-firm power during off-peak hours, the federal agency said Thursday.
BPA also placed a 200 megawatt (MW) limit on all sales during the first six and last two hours of the day.

For Friday, firm deliveries to both the Northwest and California-Oregon (COB) and Nevada-Oregon (NOB) borders during a block of light-load hours (0100-0600 and 2300-2400 PDT) were offered at $17.00 per megawatt hour (MWH), up from $15.00.
BPA offered non-firm power between 0100 and 0500 PDT on Friday at $17.00 per MWh, up from $15.00-16.00 for Thursday pre-schedulings.
BPA continued to offer block power during heavy load hours at $18.00 per MWh in the Northwest and $19.50 at COB/NOB.
Prices for non-firm power between 0600 and 2400 PDT were also unchanged at $18.50 (Northwest) and $20.00 (COB/NOB), although the hours were widened from Thursday's 0700-2200 PDT.
